I've had success with this recipe and if you roll them thin enough, you can eat them without soaking first.

  • 3 cups flour
  • 2 tsp salt
  • 1 cup water

Set your oven at 375. Makes 9ish (depending on how you cut them ) at about 150 calories each.

Mix the dry ingredients.

Slowly mix in water until you get a non-sticky dough

Roll with rolling pin until you get it between 1/4 and 1/2 inch thick. The thinner it is, the more likely you're going to be able to chomp on these without breaking your teeth.

Poke at least 4 holes in each one. I've seen recipes call for using a nail (hardcore, man) but you can use skewers, chopsticks, whatever. The holes need to be clean through because they allow it to dry out during baking.

Bake for 30 minutes (but watch them), flip and bake 30 more minutes.

They should be a light brown or tan color and hard as a rock.

If you're not planning on keeping them for forever, you can add honey for flavor (to your taste) but lower the temp to 200 and bake for an additional 30 minutes.
